author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Class sweep of the finding this change fixes. A repo-wide grep for `@RequestParam` and `PageRequest.of` across src/main/java returns exactly two pagination entry points: OwnerController (fixed here) and VetController, which still passes an unclamped `page` into `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)`. GET /vets.html?page=0 therefore still throws IllegalArgumentException, and templates/error.html renders the raw `${message}` attribute, so the exception text reaches the browser -- the information-disclosure defect REQ-SYS-002 names ('no exception message, stack trace, or other internal detail'). Out of scope for REQ-OWN-002 and pre-existing, so not blocking this change; the scope question is whether the sibling route gets a follow-up slice or is accepted as a known defect.

approved_aspects: Clamp is total over the int domain: Math.max(page, 1) admits Integer.MIN_VALUE, 0, and negatives without special-casing, so no untrusted value reaches PageRequest.of below zero

No arithmetic overflow introduced: requestedPage >= 1 makes `page - 1` non-negative, and the upper end (page = Integer.MAX_VALUE) yields a valid PageRequest whose offset is computed as a long, returning an empty page rather than throwing

Untrusted `page` stays typed as int end to end; the value reaches the view only as the numeric `currentPage` model attribute, so the Thymeleaf preprocessing expressions `__${currentPage - 1}__` and `__${currentPage + 1}__` in owners/ownersList.html cannot be steered into expression injection
No injection surface touched: data access remains a Spring Data derived query with a bound Pageable, no string-concatenated SQL, and the lastName path is unchanged
No secrets, credentials, tokens, or keys introduced in either changed file; no new dependency, so no supply-chain delta to verify for this pass

Test addition drives the boundary through the real MVC binding stack via MockMvc and asserts the clamped currentPage for both 0 and a negative value, covering the untrusted-input boundary this change exists to close

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: New test `processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage` names itself after the controller method it calls, not the behavior it verifies. testing-principles.md § Test Naming requires the BDD school (`the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`) for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward, and this test is new in this changeset.

The test body loops over `List.of("0", "-3")` with a `for` loop instead of using `@ParameterizedTest`. testing-principles.md § Test Structure bars loops in test bodies, and the checklist's own AUTOFIX list flags 'Missing @ParameterizedTest for repetitive cases' by name. The loop also means a failure on page=0 hides whether page=-3 would have failed too.
findings.fix: Convert to `@ParameterizedTest` with `@ValueSource(strings = {"0", "-3"})` (or `@CsvSource` with a comment per case), taking the page value as a method parameter.

approved_aspects: Both documented boundary values (page=0, page=-3) for the clamp are exercised
Test asserts on the actual model attribute (`currentPage`) the production fix sets, not an implementation detail
MockMvc used per the project's sanctioned-mock policy; no new mocking of internal code
Full suite passes (./gradlew test) with the new test included

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: OwnerController.processFindForm now guarantees a specific boundary behavior — a page parameter below 1 shows the first page instead — covered by the new test processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage. The Owner records section's Edge cases list (docs/prd.md:71-74) already documents a sibling input-boundary case (edge case 1: an all-spaces search behaves as empty) but says nothing about invalid page numbers, so a reader relying on the PRD alone would not know this behavior is guaranteed rather than incidental. Recommend adding a new numbered edge case under REQ-OWN-002 stating the page-below-1 behavior in plain given/when/then language, consistent with the existing edge-case bullets.

approved_aspects: No PRD-boundary violations, no internal code references introduced, no cross-document ID or anchor breakage in the diff

The new FIRST_PAGE constant is a trivial, non-cross-cutting local literal and does not require an entry in system-design.md's Constants table, consistent with the existing treatment of the sibling page-size local variable

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner listing page below one to first page

blast_radius.note: Two files, six hunks, one controller method plus its test; the prod edit is confined to OwnerController.processFindForm and the only new symbol is a private FIRST_PAGE constant, with no sensitive paths, no config, no schema, and no shared helper touched.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks, Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) is total over the int domain and both downstream consumers of the raw parameter (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) were switched to the clamped value with no residual use of the unclamped page left in the method; the only nit is that the local requestedPage actually holds the effective page rather than the requested one.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized test drives page=0 and page=-3 through the real MVC binding stack and asserts the currentPage model attribute equals 1, so it fails against the unclamped implementation (PageRequest.of(-1) throws) rather than restating it; the two boundary values are exercised independently after the loop was replaced with @ValueSource.

reviewer_hedging.note: Two of the four approvals carry open clarify findings rather than being clean: security-reviewer approved while reporting that the identical unclamped-page defect still lives in VetController:45,61 and that the raw exception message reaches the browser via templates/error.html, and doc-reviewer approved while noting the new guaranteed behavior is undocumented in the PRD edge cases; test-reviewer's approval came only on a second pass after two tested-as-spec bar-clause findings were reworked.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations and zero build retries, and the diff matches the requirement's stated surface exactly - the change deliberately did not follow the security reviewer's pointer into VetController, leaving the sibling route to a follow-up slice instead of widening this one.

rationale: The fix itself is small, total over its input domain, and genuinely tested at the boundary. What deserves a look is the residual the reviewers flagged and nobody closed: the same unclamped-page bug still throws on GET /vets.html?page=0, with the exception text rendered to the browser. Decide follow-up before merging.
